title: Co-transplantation of Human Ovarian Tissue with Engineered Endothelial Cells: A Cell-based Strategy Combining Accelerated Perfusion with Direct Paracrine Delivery
protocol: Collect the ovarian tissue and rinse with a sterile saline solution.
Place the ovary in a sterile container.
Pour Leibovitz's L-15 medium until the ovary is completely immersed in the medium.
Close and seal the container.
Transport the container on ice.
Prepare 100 mL of freezing solution using DMSO as a cryo-protectant.
Add 69.64 mL Leibovitz's L-15 medium to the solution.
Add 17.66 mL fetal bovine serum (FBS) to the solution.
Add 3.42 g of sucrose to create a final concentration of 0.1 mol/L in the solution.
Add 10.65 mL DMSO to create a final concentration of 1.5 mol/L in the solution.
Add 1 mL antibiotic-antimycotic solution to the mixture.
Filter the medium using a 150 mL filter unit with a 0.2 µm pore size.
Store the filtered medium at 4 °C.
Sterilize surgical tools using an autoclave programmed for a wrapped solids sterilization cycle.

Set sterile surgical tools in the biosafety cabinet: scalpel with blade number 21, sharp fine curved scissors and forceps of various sizes (long about 150 mm length, two medium-sized about 110 mm length).
Wear sterile gloves.
Open the container within the biosafety cabinet.
Take the ovary and place it in a 150 mm Petri dish.
Pour cold medium prepared in step 2.1.1 on top of the ovary to prevent dehydration.
Isolate the ovary from any residual tissue and rinse it with cold medium until it is devoid of tissue and blood.
Place the ovary in a clean 150 mm Petri dish.
Add cold medium prepared in step 2.1.1 until the ovary is half submerged in it.
Dissect the ovarian tissue by bisecting the ovary.
Remove the medulla first using sharp dissection with curved fine scissors.
Scrape away the medulla using a sterile scalpel with blade number 21.
Proceed until the cortical tissue is 1-1.5 mm in thickness.
Cut cortical tissue into slivers of 2-3 mm in width.
Label cryovials (1.8 mL).
Add 1.5 mL of freezing solution to each vial.
Transfer one cortical strip to a vial containing the freezing solution.
Equilibrate the cortical strip for 20 min on a rotating plate at 4 °C with gentle agitation.
Load cryovials into a programmable planer freezer starting at 0 °C.
Cool at 2 °C/min to -7 °C and maintain this temperature for 10 min.
Perform manual seeding by touching each vial with a cotton tip immersed in liquid nitrogen (LN2).
Continue cooling at 0.3 °C/min until sample temperature reaches -40 °C.
Cool at 10 °C/min from -40 °C to -140 °C.
Transfer cryovials to the dewar for storage in LN2 (-196 °C).
Place a piece of plastic paraffin film at the bottom of a 50 mm Petri dish.
Spray the film with 70% Ethanol until completely covered.
Leave the Petri dishes overnight in the biosafety cabinet.
Aspirate ethanol from the Petri dish containing plastic paraffin film within the biosafety cabinet.
Leave the Petri dish partially open until ethanol evaporates completely.
Close the lid of the Petri dish when the plastic paraffin film is dry.
Keep the Petri dish within the biosafety cabinet.
Label wells of a 6 well plate accordingly.
Prepare 100 mL of BTS: Mix Leibovitz's L-15 medium 79 mL with FBS 20 mL and Antibiotic-Antimycotic solution 1 mL.
Filter the prepared BTS using a 0.22 μm filter system.
Prepare 10 mL of BTS with 0.1 mol/L Sucrose: Scale 0.342 g of Sucrose, add to 10 mL of BTS, and agitate gently until dissolved.
Filter the solution containing Sucrose using a syringe filter 0.22 μm.
Cover tubes containing DMSO with aluminum foil.
Keep refrigerated until use.
Take out a vial containing frozen ovarian tissue from LN2 dewar and keep at room temperature for 30 seconds.
Wipe the vial clean using tissue paper.
Immerse the vial in a 30 °C water bath for 1-2 minutes until content is thawed.
Open the vial and place cortical strip in the first well containing 3 mL of the prepared solution (0.1 mol/L Sucrose+ 1 mol/L DMSO).
Incubate the 6 well plate on a rotating plate at 4 °C for 5 min.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil during incubation.
Transfer the cortical strip into the second well containing 3 mL of solution (0.1 mol/L Sucrose + 0.5 mol/L DMSO).
Incubate the 6 well plate on a rotating plate at 4 °C for 5 min.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil during incubation.
Transfer the cortical strip into the third well containing 4 mL of solution (BTS with 0.1 mol/L Sucrose).
Incubate on a rotating plate at 4 °C for 5 min.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil during incubation.
Transfer the cortical strip into the fourth well containing 4 mL of BTS solution.
Incubate on a rotating plate at 4 °C for 5 min.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil during incubation.
Transfer the cortical strip into the last well containing 4 mL of cold medium.
Keep thawed ovarian tissue on ice until transplantation.
Prepare 25 mL of 20 mmol/L HEPES buffer in 0.9% saline.
Filter and store the HEPES buffer at 4 °C.
Dissolve 1 g of Fibrinogen into 20 mL of 20 mmol/L HEPES buffer by slowly mixing over several hours at 37 °C.
Prepare 1 mL of CaCl₂ at a concentration of 1 mol/L.
Filter and store the CaCl₂ solution at 4 °C.
Filter the solution through a 0.45 µm syringe filter.
Filter the solution through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Aliquot the solution into 200 μL portions and store at -20°C.
Add 2.5 mL of 0.9% sterile saline to 250 U of Thrombin.
Gently shake until the Thrombin solution is completely dissolved.
Label 1.7 mL micro-centrifuge tubes.
Filter the Thrombin solution through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Aliquot 50 μL into micro-centrifuge tubes and store at -80°C.
Prepare a Fibrin clot of 70 µL, obtaining a final concentration of 10 mg/mL fibrinogen and 5 U/mL Thrombin.
Add 360 µL of 20 mmol/L HEPES Buffer in 0.9% saline solution to the aliquoted 200 μL of Fibrinogen stock.
Mix by gentle pipetting.
Keep it on ice.
Add 148.7 µL of DMEM to the aliquoted 50 µL of Thrombin stock.
Mix by gentle pipetting.
Add 1.3 µL of 1 mol/L CaCl2.
Mix by gentle pipetting.
Keep it on ice.
Prepare a single cell suspension in a third micro-centrifuge tube.
Detach the engineered endothelial cells from the plate using an enzyme cell detachment medium.
Spin down the cells and count them using a hemocytometer with a cover glass.
Use 20,000 cells per every 1 mm² of ovarian tissue.
Calculate the area of ovarian tissue in mm² based on cell count.
Resuspend engineered endothelial cells in basic medium (DMEM) to reach a total volume of 16.8 μL.
Place a piece of ovarian tissue on a sterile gauze sponge to dry it for a few seconds.
Place the dried ovarian tissue on top of the plastic paraffin film within the 50 mm Petri dish.
Add 39.2 µL of the Fibrinogen solution into the cell suspension, mix by gentle pipetting.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Add 14 µL of the Thrombin solution to the mixture and mix gently once.
Work fast.
Place the mixture on top of the ovarian tissue in the form of an elongated droplet.
Place the Petri dish with the clot in the incubator at 37 °C.
Observe effects of anesthesia; loss of consciousness, slow and regular breaths.
Transfer the mouse to the nose cone to maintain anesthesia.
Adjust vaporizer to deliver 1-3% isoflurane depending on vital signs.
Verify absence of pedal or tail reflex.
Increase isoflurane until pedal or tail reflex is absent if present.
Trim the mouse's back hair from the tail up to the clavicles line using an electric hair trimmer.
Place the mouse in a prone position on the surgical platform.
Fix the nose cone to the surgical platform using surgical tape.
Gently tape the mouse's limbs to the surgical platform using 1.25 cm-wide surgical paper tape.
Use sterile lubricant jelly and insert a thermometer PR.
Fix the thermometer by taping it to the surgical platform using a 1.25 cm wide perforated plastic surgical tape.
Tape the tail to the surgical platform using a 2.5 cm wide surgical paper tape.
Heat the mouse using an infrared or hot water heating pad.
Monitor the mouse's body temperature throughout the procedure.
Keep body temperature within the range of 35-37 °C.
Clean the trimmed area with a sterile Povidone-Iodine Solution swab stick and wipe using sterile alcohol prep.
Repeat step 6.9 twice more.
Place a drop of sterile ocular lubricant vet ointment over each of the mouse's eyes to protect from dehydration and damage to the cornea.
Cover the mouse using a sterile surgical drape.
Inject Buprenorphine (1 mg/Kg) sub-cutaneous (S/C).
Perform a longitudinal medial dorsal incision using a scalpel (blade #21).
Perform a bilateral oophorectomy using a dorsal approach.
Free subcutaneous connective tissue by blunt dissection with scissors.
Make an incision in the fascia laterally to the midline to reach the peritoneal cavity.
Gently grasp the ovarian fat pad and ovary with tweezers and pull it out of the abdominal cavity.
Ligate the ovary and fat pad using a 4/0 monofilament absorbable suture at the base, distal to the fallopian tube.
Clip the ovary distal to the ligature and ensure no bleeding from the stump.
Replace tissue into the abdominal cavity and suture the fascia with a 6/0 braided absorbable suture.
Repeat stages for contralateral side starting from grasping the ovarian fat pad and ovary.
Create a horizontal incision in the fascia above the Gluteus Maximus, fitting the clot dimensions.
Open scissors underneath the fascia to create a pocket within this space.
Place one piece of encapsulated cortical tissue into the created pocket.
Suture the fascia using a 6/0 braided absorbable suture.
Repeat stages for contralateral side starting from making an incision in the fascia above Gluteus Maximus.
Close the dorsal wall using simple interrupted stitches with a 4/0 monofilament absorbable suture.
Inject Lidocaine 0.5% subcutaneously at the incision site, 1.2 mL/Kg.
Clean skin with sterile alcohol prep.
Turn off the isoflurane while monitoring the mouse's temperature.
Provide 1-2 min of O2 without isoflurane.
Continue warming the mouse until it starts to move and regain consciousness.
Place the mouse in a clean recovery cage.
House the mouse separately until surgical wound healing is complete.
Inject Buprenorphine (1 mg/Kg) S/C as needed every 8-12 h for 24 h postoperatively.
Keep mice in separate cages with autoclaved food, water, bedding, and cages.
Maintain cages in a pressurized ventilated room.
Use personal protective equipment when handling the mice.
